Ryan Watkins on Why Annualizing 30-Day Revenue to Value Hyperliquid Is Flawed
> Annualizing 30-day revenue to value cyclical crypto businesses like Hyperliquid is fundamentally flawed.
> He argues the right approach is forward earnings analysis that accounts for the cycle, new business lines, and exponential growth, which makes HYPE cheap rather than expensive.
Source:
https://twitter.com/RyanWatkins_/status/2090082801143939164

tweet.text:
The way everyone thinks about forward revenue estimates in crypto is flawed.

Industry standard today is to annualize 30D revenue, which may be fine for getting to a run-rate number, but inadequate for projecting growth.

It’s also particularly silly for cyclical businesses, especially in a trough period.

Take Hyperliquid as an example:

1) Annualizing 30D revenue during a cyclical trough in its core crypto markets is silly unless you believe we will never enter a bull market again

2) Annualizing Hyperliquid’s 30D revenue and using it as the foundation for a forward earnings estimate is short-sighted for a business that’s growing exponentially and constantly introducing new business lines

For example. If you annualized revenue at any point in Q2’25 last year you would’ve extrapolated trough volume, and wouldn’t have factored in future products, upgrades, and partnerships.

Link
The Treasury issued proposed rules clarifying when stablecoin issuers need a federal or state license. The framework takes effect January 18, 2027, and a 60-day public comment period is now open.

Matters because: It adds regulatory clarity for stablecoins, which could support institutional adoption over time, even if near-term market impact is limited.
